instructions.content: Waves enforce ordering, not scheduling: a wave boundary exists only where a real dependency forces sequential execution, and parallel is the default
One branch per parallel workstream: each phase in a parallel wave gets its own branch and worktree, and agents never share a working tree
The wave document is the source of truth: status lives in the wave plan, not in individual task files
Gates before advancing: ALWAYS verify the current wave fully passes before starting the next one
Every wave boundary must be a safe deploy point; avoid stranded consumers, premature consumers and breaking contract changes by using must land together grouping or expand-contract sequencing
Use Mode A for new requirements or an existing flat plan, and Mode B when a wave document exists and tasks have been completed
Extract every task with an ID, description and explicit dependencies; if none are stated, infer from logical ordering (a test task depends on its implementation task)
Build the dependency DAG from the extracted tasks
Assign waves: Wave 1 is tasks with no dependencies; Wave N is tasks whose dependencies are all in waves 1 to N-1
Mark a wave with more than one independent task parallel, and a wave with one task or tasks that must run in order sequential
Apply the safe intermediate state check to every wave boundary and merge both sides into a single must land together wave if existing functionality would break
Write the wave document as plans/<plan-slug>.md in the context directory using the wave-format reference
Validate that every task appears in exactly one wave and no wave contains tasks that depend on each other
In Mode B, read the wave document, run the completed wave's Verification commands, update statuses, append DONE to the wave heading, announce the next unblocked wave and its mode, and save
Mark a blocked task with the Blocked status and add a BLOCKED note
NEVER put dependent tasks in the same wave
NEVER label a wave parallel if it contains only one task
NEVER advance to Wave N+1 before Wave N verification passes
NEVER track status inside individual task files
NEVER invent dependencies that are not stated in the requirements
NEVER create an unsafe intermediate deploy state at a wave boundary
ALWAYS run the verification checklist before declaring a wave done
Do not use the skill when the plan has only 1 to 2 tasks with no parallelism, or when all tasks are sequential; a checklist or single branch is simpler
